\title{Data Decides Whether, Location Decides How and How Fast: Repairing a Planted Shortcut in GPT-2}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Sonu Akash, Sidhant Holla, Siddhant Khurdiya, Piyush Shiv}
\IEEEauthorblockA{Department of Computer Science and Engineering (AI \& ML)\\
PES University, Bengaluru, India}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Interpretability tools can show where a behaviour happens inside a language model. Does that location tell us where to
repair it? We study a shortcut with known ground truth: GPT-2 small learns IMDB sentiment while an invented actor name,
planted in 5\% of the training reviews, always comes with the same label. The logit lens, block swaps and activation
patching agree that the name reaches the answer only in the last three blocks. \emph{Whether} retraining removes the
shortcut is decided by the repair data: one epoch on clean data removes it from any single block, because the clean
data shows each name with both labels, and without these counter-examples no block removes more than
\ccNoNamesMaxFullFT{} of it in any seed. \emph{How} and \emph{how fast} a block removes it depend on location: after 100 steps,
block~2 has removed \budgetBTwoStepHundredFullFTRange{} of the shortcut and block~10 \budgetBTenStepHundredFullFTRange,
and across experiments block~0 and the later blocks are fast while blocks 1--5 are slow, a pattern we noticed after the
fact. The tools point to the late blocks but never to block~0, which repairs the shortcut by changing only what the name
tokens pass on. At the zero-training end, carrying the layer-9 state forward to the output removes
\pSixBEqLNineRemovedFullFTRange{} of the shortcut at an accuracy cost of \pSixBEqLNineDropFullFTRange, more than the
same dose from any other layer. LoRA rank~64 shows the same pattern; for memorized wrong labels, which share no cue that
the repair data could contradict, only one block works.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
shortcut learning, interpretability, logit lens, activation patching, model repair, early exit, GPT-2
\end{IEEEkeywords}
